heading: PNG Compressor Online to Reduce File Size and Keep Transparency
introduction:
PNG images are widely used for logos, screenshots, diagrams, icons and digital graphics. One of their main advantages is the ability to preserve transparent backgrounds. This makes PNG a useful format when an image needs to appear over different colors or backgrounds without showing a solid rectangle around it.

However, PNG files can become large, especially when they contain detailed graphics, high-resolution screenshots or many colors. Large files may take longer to upload, use additional storage and increase the size of website resources.

File Compresser provides an online PNG Compressor that helps reduce PNG file size directly in your browser. You can choose different optimization modes, compare the original and processed image and keep control of the transparency and dimensions. The tool processes files on your device, so there is no need to upload your images to an external server or install additional software.

sections.heading: What Is a PNG Compressor?
sections.body:
A PNG compressor is a tool that optimizes the way image data is stored in a PNG file. It can reduce unnecessary data and, depending on the selected method, reduce the number of colors used in the image.

PNG uses lossless compression at the file-format level. However, a PNG optimization process can also use color reduction. These are two different approaches.

Lossless optimization preserves the decoded image pixels. Color reduction changes image colors to create a smaller file, although transparency can still be preserved. File Compresser provides separate options so you can choose the approach that suits your image.

sections.heading: How to Compress PNG Images Online
sections.body:
You can reduce PNG file size without using a desktop image editing program.

Follow these steps:

1. Open the PNG Compressor page.
2. Select a PNG image from your device.
3. Wait for the image validation process.
4. Review the available compression modes.
5. Choose Lossless, Smart, Maximum or Target Size.
6. Enable resizing only if you need different dimensions.
Start processing.
7. Compare the original and processed file sizes.
8. Check the image, edges and transparent areas before downloading.

The tool keeps the original image dimensions unless you specifically enable resizing.
